- Overestimate prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.10) in the last 3–5 days, model tends to overreact; dampen forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.30) and price is falling, model often undercorrects; add a 2–5% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- Forecast mean reversion is weak in the first 7–10 days; if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative, model should not assume immediate reversal.
- If model shows a sharp upward spike followed by a steep drop, reduce the magnitude of the drop by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.
- For horizon >15 days, model tends to underestimate downward moves; add 1–3% upward bias to counteract mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model should not forecast a sharp rebound unless sentiment turns positive within 2 days.
